subject.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock

question: May runtime auth start a retry after the 360-second deadline while the original provider/keychain/OAuth operation remains uncancelled, relying on generation and ownership guards only to prevent local stale writes?
rationale: This is a deliberate availability-versus-provider-side concurrency tradeoff. Tests demonstrate local lane recovery and stale-write protection, but they cannot establish the idempotency, refresh-token rotation, or side-effect semantics of every underlying provider and keychain operation.

options.title: Require an explicit overlap contract
options.body: Keep the deadline design only after the auth owners document which provider operations may overlap after abandonment and add targeted proof for the supported refresh semantics.

options.title: Keep exclusive ownership until settlement
options.body: Change retries to wait for or otherwise serialize the abandoned operation, accepting slower recovery to avoid concurrent external refresh side effects.

options.title: Accept the local-only guard boundary
options.body: Land the current design while explicitly accepting that it guarantees local state safety and lane recovery, not cancellation or provider-side serialization.

recommendation.title: Require an explicit overlap contract
recommendation.body: Keep the deadline design only after the auth owners document which provider operations may overlap after abandonment and add targeted proof for the supported refresh semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the current auth-profile storage and upgrade boundary most affected by this decision.
